info.title: LiteGate API
info.description: LiteGate LLM gateway: /v1/* are gateway endpoints (gateway API key); /api/* are console management endpoints (console session; no authentication when login is disabled).

gatewayKey.description: Gateway API key (lgk-…); /v1/messages also accepts the x-api-key header

consoleSession.name: lg_session
consoleSession.description: Console login session; Authorization: Bearer lgs-… also works

post.description: Selects the upstream by model (route name); upstreams may speak the OpenAI or Anthropic protocol and are converted automatically. Streaming uses SSE. Request tags: header X-LiteGate-Tags: a,b (OpenAI / Responses formats may also use metadata.tags), merged with the key's default tags and used for per-tag usage and budgets; metadata.tags is not forwarded upstream.

parameters.name: X-LiteGate-Tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated request tags (at most 8, each ≤ 64 characters, limited to A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . : / -)

parameters.name: X-LiteGate-Session
parameters.description: Session identifier (used for session affinity and for reusing rule decisions within a session); if absent, taken in turn from x-session-affinity, X-Claude-Code-Session-Id, session-id, or the body's prompt_cache_key / metadata.user_id; if none is present, derived from the key, model name, system prompt and first user message

parameters.name: traceparent
parameters.description: W3C Trace Context (version 00); when OTLP export is enabled the gateway's spans join this trace

parameters.name: X-LiteGate-Client
parameters.description: Self-reported client tool name (≤ 32 characters, limited to A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -); if absent, claude-code, codex, opencode, openai-sdk and anthropic-sdk are recognized from request headers, otherwise other

post.description: The key may be sent in x-api-key or Authorization: Bearer; anthropic-version / anthropic-beta are passed through to Anthropic upstreams. post.description: A name ending in * is a wildcard route (any prefix, e.g. openrouter/*, claude-*; a lone * is the catch-all), and writing * as the target upstream model substitutes the remaining part. aliases are exact model names that also route to this route (globally unique). Matching order: route name → alias → longest-prefix wildcard. options: cache_ttl_s (response cache seconds), strategy (weighted | order | rotate | usage | smart | pace, ordering within the same priority), affinity (auto | session | off, session affinity), rules (list of rules: {when: {min_tokens, max_tokens, images, thinking, client, tags, hours, intent}, use: route name} or {when, skip: [credential id]}, at most 16), classifier (route name of the intent classification model); null removes the option.

post.summary: Structured decision (TypeSafe System One, e.g. Bailian decision-model-preview)
post.description: Returns, in a single forward pass, the results and probability distributions of classification (choice), yes/no (noul) and ordinal scoring (score), without generating text. Uses only openai-protocol targets and is passed through to the credential's {base_url}/systemone (Bailian's base_url is …/compatible-mode/v1, local Laya is http://host:port/v1); model is replaced with the upstream model and the model in the response is changed back to the requested route name; middleware is not applied. Billed per input token (catalog override cost.input). Simply point the TypeSafe SDK's base_url at the gateway.

get.description: Per-route request / reroute / error counts and clients over the last 5 minutes, in-flight requests, and the live state of every candidate target of the selected route (?route=, defaults to the busiest one). The live event stream is GET /api/live/stream (text/event-stream, console identity): it first pushes a state event, then request_start, decision, attempt_start, attempt_end and request_end events.

get.summary: List gateway middleware (with call statistics) and available implementations
get.description: Middleware runs at three points: on_request (after the request body is parsed, before routing), on_event (before a streaming frame is written to the client) and on_response (before a non-streaming reply is written to the client). If a hook errors or times out, the data passes through unchanged. impls lists the available implementations with their supported hooks and configuration examples.

get.description: When an upstream rejects a parameter or usage with 400 / 422, the gateway records {credential, upstream model, feature} and rewrites later requests automatically. Features: temperature, top_p, thinking_off, enable_thinking_sync, prefill, output_config, json_schema.
